interpretation: The zero-trade source backtest was not accepted as a gate verdict. Every independent leader-shock episode and rejected SOL/XRP target was reconstructed before viewing the future path.

The predicted direction was already slightly wrong before costs. The source gates therefore did not hide a positive opportunity engine; they suppressed a relationship whose gross response was approximately zero or negative.
Stable seesaw was the least bad state, but its mean 15-minute gross response was only 0.056 bps, far below realistic entry and exit costs.
Large positive rejected examples existed, but they were a selected minority inside distributions with negative mean response and cannot justify a hindsight filter.
